chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja'far ibn Bashir from al-Haytham ibn 'Urwah al-Tamimi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I carried my wife, then I performed Tawaf with her, and she was ill.' I said to him, 'I performed Tawaf with her at the House during the obligatory Tawaf, and at As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and I counted that for my own self.' He said, 'Does that suffice for you?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.احْتَسَبْتُ: I counted/reckoned (as a reward or fulfillment of duty)
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)

ai.seo_question: Does carrying an ill wife during Hajj rituals suffice for her obligatory Tawaf and Sa'i?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that carrying an ill wife to perform the obligatory Tawaf and Sa'i suffices for her religious obligation, establishing the principle of vicarious performance (niyabah) for those unable to move independently. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding physical incapacity, allowing a healthy family member to act as a proxy to ensure the ritual is completed without burdening the patient. The narration underscores the communal and familial support structures inherent in fulfilling individual worship duties.
